spans.text: Sampling and assignment
spans.quality: native-text; line-level location; formulas may need visual checking

spans.text:
A population is the group about which a study wants to draw conclusions. A sample is the group
actually observed. Random sampling is a method of selecting observations from a population
using a random mechanism with defined selection probabilities. It can support population
inference, subject to the sampling design, nonresponse, and other limitations.
spans.quality: native-text; line-level location; formulas may need visual checking

spans.text:
Random assignment is a method of assigning study participants to treatment conditions using a
random mechanism. It aims to make treatment groups comparable in expectation before
treatment. It does not guarantee identical groups in every realized experiment.
spans.quality: native-text; line-level location; formulas may need visual checking

spans.text:
Random sampling and random assignment answer different questions. Sampling concerns who
enters the study; assignment concerns which treatment participants receive. A study can use
either, both, or neither.
spans.quality: native-text; line-level location; formulas may need visual checking

spans.text:
Example: Students volunteer for a study of a study-planning app. The researchers randomly
assign the volunteers to use the app or to continue their usual routine. This is random
assignment within a volunteer sample. The design can support a causal comparison for the
study participants under appropriate assumptions, but the volunteers may differ from the wider
student population.
spans.quality: native-text; line-level location; formulas may need visual checking

spans.text:
Example: Researchers randomly sample students from a university roster and observe their
existing study habits. This is random sampling without random assignment of habits. A
representative sample does not by itself turn an observed relationship between habits and
grades into a causal effect.
spans.quality: native-text; line-level location; formulas may need visual checking

spans.text:
Questions to explain
Which process affects group comparability? Which process affects population coverage? Can a
randomized experiment still have limited generalizability?

spans.text: Association, confounding, and limits
spans.quality: native-text; line-level location; formulas may need visual checking

spans.text:
An association means two variables vary together in the observed data. A causal claim says that
changing one variable would change another under specified conditions. An association alone
does not establish such a claim.
spans.quality: native-text; line-level location; formulas may need visual checking

spans.text:
A confounder is a variable related to the treatment or exposure and the outcome in a way that
can distort the observed association. In a study of app use and grades, prior motivation may
influence both the decision to use the app and academic performance.
spans.quality: native-text; line-level location; formulas may need visual checking

spans.text:
Random assignment addresses systematic pre-treatment differences between groups in
expectation. It does not automatically solve every problem: differential dropout, noncompliance,
measurement problems, or interference between participants can still complicate interpretation.
spans.quality: native-text; line-level location; formulas may need visual checking

spans.text:
Suppose volunteers randomly assigned to the app group have higher average grades at the end
of a well-conducted study. This is stronger evidence for a causal effect in that study than a
simple observation that app users have higher grades. Extending the result to all college
students requires considering the population, sample, implementation, and setting.
spans.quality: native-text; line-level location; formulas may need visual checking

spans.text:
A careful conclusion distinguishes the design's causal support from the scope of generalization.
“Random assignment” does not mean “random sample,” and “random sample” does not mean
“causation established.”
spans.quality: native-text; line-level location; formulas may need visual checking

spans.text:
Questions to explain
How could motivation create an association without an app effect? Why is random assignment
useful even though realized groups may differ by chance? What additional question remains when
generalizing beyond volunteers?
